title: Madras School System and AI Learning Share Similarity
summary:
Madras School education system (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madras_School) that was the bedrock of mass public structured education in the late 18-19th century has several similarities on how AI is trained today.

They both ensures that knowledge dissemination is free.

The similarities they share are as follows

1) Madras school & AI distillation (Teacher-Student models) encourages Students to teach others instead of just teachers thereby reducing cost.

2) Madras school & Reinforcement learning rewards or awards penalty scores based on the assessment/feedback.

3) Both systems ultimately ended in rote learning and hallucinations.

The other day when I noticed that several leading professors of top universities were sharing their top courses for free on YT. I immediately remembered our education system (Madras School) and how it had a profound impact in today's education system especially public mass elementary schooling system. It is also notable that today's AI training took a leaf out of it. Those professors were indeed trying to bring Madras school system to the Universities by free knowledge dissemination that too in this AI era, which is commendable.

But the current commercial education system is a stark difference from the Madras school which was designed for the mass and was affordable. But today's education and research is full of competition and highly unaffordable which was not the case in the early 19th century.

Finally, I would like to conclude that the commercial education (training teachers) and proprietary SOTA frontier models both gate keep their highest tier capabilities behind high tuition or API paywalls, whereas open weights models and the Madras System prioritize broad, low cost knowledge dissemination.

title: Ask HN: What positive impact has AI had in the past 5 years?
summary:
I asked myself this question this morning and I swear I couldn't find one single thing.

We still have all the problems we had before AI. AI did not solve the climate collapse, did not cure cancer, did not figure society-altering new technologies, did not make politics not suck anymore, did not solve our anxieties...

If anything, we're all just more anxious today. It succeeded at making my work toxic because of the cyber warfare paranoia, I guess.

AI successfully blew and continues to blow all the benchmarks it's been trained to blow. It makes long mathematical proofs nobody can read or verify about problems nobody cares about. Great?

So… can someone list things that AI has genuinely improved?

If there are none, why do we tolerate it?

title: Tell HN: /tmp is hogging your RAM on Ubuntu 26
summary:
As a Ubuntu user, it was just brought to my attention that /tmp is now mounted on tmpfs (aka your RAM).

Coding agents, like Claude Code, use /tmp as a scratchpad for files, model weights, etc.

Therefore, if you have RAM constraints, consider setting CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR to e.g. ~/.claude/tmp

title: I open-sourced an AI loop for RISC-V CPU design months prior to OpenAI
summary:
Back in April, I built auto-arch-tournament (https://github.com/FeSens/auto-arch-tournament) to explore a question I’m still curious about: how well can different AI models improve a RISC-V CPU? I’ve been tracking the results on HWEBench(https://hwebench.com/v2).

It’s fun to see OpenAI exploring a similar question in today’s chip design post(https://openai.com/index/advancing-chip-design-with-our-models/). If you’d like to try an experiment yourself, you can run the research loop from the repo.
